messages:
ashok: Headline — saw a sudden retry/burst on svc/ml-infer in us-west-2. Traffic collapsed onto pod-3 and its GPU spiked to 98% for ~2m. Errors = 502/504s, huge token tail latencies.

lina: saw it on dashboards too. Per-route breakdown shows 87% of requests to pod-3 for ~10k reqs/min window. Total cluster load steady, just this service acting weird. :thinking_face:

jon: any recent deploys or rollout for ml-infer? Canary config?

ashok: no deploys in last 24h. Canary was healthy. Autoscaler didn't trigger. Kubernetes events show repeated readinessProbe failures for pod-1/pod-2 just before spike.

maria: readiness flaps -> kube-proxy/ipvs might drop destinations and then re-add them. If ipvs hash redistributed badly you can get a thundering herd to the same backend.

lina: good call. I pulled ipvs stats from node where pod-3 landed: 

```
# ipvsadm -Ln --stats
IP Virtual Server version 1.2.1 (size=4096)
Prot LocalAddress:Port Scheduler Flags
  -> RemoteAddress:Port           Forward Weight ActiveConn InActConn
TCP  10.2.5.12:8080 rr
  -> 10.1.3.7:8080                 Route    1      10234      12
  -> 10.1.4.9:8080                 Route    1       123       1
  -> 10.1.5.3:8080                 Route   10      89321      34
```

lina: that output shows pod-3 (10.1.5.3) with ~89k active connections vs others near zero.

jon: conn patterns like that usually mean either sticky session affinitization or conntrack entries not expiring after endpoints were rebalanced. Any conntrack saturation/logs?

ashok: node /proc/net/nf_conntrack count is high on the node with pod-3. grep shows many entries for svc IP:port -> pod-3. conntrack logs show a lot of TCP_FIN_DELAY entries.

maria: also noticed an RDMA NIC flapping alert on that node minutes earlier (link up/down). RDMA events can cause transient endpoint unreachability at kernel level which makes kube-proxy rehash destinations.

lina: hypothesis: brief readiness flaps + RDMA NIC bounce -> kube-proxy/ipvs removed endpoints then re-added; hash redistribution + client retries from LB caused most new flows to pick the hot pod. Retries amplified the herd.

jon: suggested immediate mitigations: 1) drain pod-3 from service routing (ipvsadm -D dest) on affected node; 2) increase readinessProbe failureThreshold temporarily; 3) tune conntrack timeout for ESTABLISHED to be lower but conservative.

ashok: performed #1 and #2: removed dest for 10.1.5.3 and bumped readiness failureThreshold from 3->10 via rollout of kube-probe config on the deployment (can revert later). After removal active connections trended down and GPU load normalized in ~45s.

maria: added small script to reconcile ipvs dest weights after readiness flaps to avoid full hash churn — not a long-term fix but prevents immediate re-add storm.

devops-bot: deploy job 3172 started: rollout ml-infer probed config -> bump readiness thresholds.

jon: follow-ups: audit kube-proxy logs across nodes for endpoint add/remove storms (kube-proxy -v=4), check whether --ipvs-scheduler changed, and evaluate enabling --ipvs-sync-period to slightly longer window to avoid thrash. Also check MTU/probe settings on RDMA NICs — if link flaps are frequent we need NIC firmware or driver fix.

ashok: filing tracking ticket ENGRT-821 (root cause investigation + longer-term fixes: conntrack tuning, kube-proxy flag review, RDMA NIC stability). I'll attach ipvs dumps and node conntrack snapshots to the ticket.

lina: noted. For cost ops: because GPU was saturated for ~2 mins and autoscaler did not react, we lost capacity headroom. Add autoscaler metric alert for sustained GPU_util > 80% for 30s.

maria: also recording a runbook step: if you see >60% traffic concentrated on single backend for >20s, run `ipvsadm -D --dest` to temporarily remove hot dest and let k8s redistribute.

ashok: thanks team. tagging @oncall for follow-through. :white_check_mark:
